title: A PDF renderer on the Mac, so scanned manual pages can be read as …
ask: May the agent install poppler (a free PDF renderer) on the Mac with Homebrew, so that a run can look at a scanned manual page instead of only its OCR text?
why: Most of the manuals are scans. This Mac has no PDF renderer (the tool is called poppler), so a run here can read only the OCR text of a scanned page, never the page itself. The text is fine for sentences and plain figures, but it loses drawings (where the engine number is, the lift pads, which connector to unplug) and scrambles tables made of marks: the 1985 maintenance table (p.0-13, 0-14) came out with its I/R/L marks in no readable column, so the inspection intervals for brakes, steering, suspension and seat belts could not be taken, and the wheel-bearing interval went in marked confirm. With the renderer a run can look at the page and read these. Without it, every scanned section is parsed from text alone and what the text cannot say is listed and left out.
options:
(a) Yes: the agent installs poppler on the Mac with Homebrew (brew install poppler). Free, about a minute, removed again with brew uninstall poppler. Scanned pages can then be read as images on the Mac. Forecloses nothing.
(b) No: nothing is installed. Scans are parsed from their OCR text only; drawings and mark tables are skipped and named in each row's result. Costs nothing; the Manual stays without those facts unless you read them off the page yourself.
(c) Not on the Mac: the pages that need looking at are left for a run on the Fedora PC, if it has a renderer. Costs nothing; those rows wait until a run happens there.
recommend: (a), unless you would rather nothing is installed on the Mac by a run
stops: 06-intake P83 (the 1985 maintenance table's inspection intervals) and every drawing and mark table in the scanned sections still to parse; the text of those sections is parsed meanwhile
